src: Muscoda Leader-Press, 13 Nov 1930, p. 1, 'Five Counties Join in Hunt for Bandits. Buried Gold Sought in Hold-up' (Newspapers.com 885469793)
tw-horrigan-boscobel-1930.st: The Muscoda Leader-Press of 13 Nov 1930 put the farm home '4 miles west of Tavera' and said the brothers had twice before defended the place against marauders drawn by reports of thousands of dollars in gold buried about the premises; they did not trust banks and had 'secreted their wealth in caches on the farm'.

set.tovw: Lead grade B: period local papers and the AP give the hidden caches, three raids and the diggers; the farmstead is placed from the c.1915 plat and the 1938 aerial and confirmed by two independent bearings; no find reported.
pinev: Farmstead-level: the 1938 WHAIFinder frame BHP-1-41 (georeferenced to about 100 m) shows a farmstead at the head of the hollow road in sec 35 T10N R3W, within about 200 m of the c.1915 plat house dots on the Clayton block; the 1940 recap says the family lived on a large farm in the town of Clayton, so this is the home place. The c.1915 Hixson plat shows the family block across the town line (167.68 ac in Scott sec 2 plus the Clayton block in secs 35-36), checked against BLM PLSS. Radius 600 m reaches the town line and the start of the Scott sec 2 land.

Second bearing: '4 miles west of Tavera' (Muscoda Leader-Press, 13 Nov 1930); Tavera Cemetery (GNIS 1575263) is at 43.2847,-90.6353, and the sec 35 farmstead pin lies 3.3 mi west of it, so the two bearings (17 mi from Boscobel; 4 mi W of Tavera) agree on the Clayton home place.
